Industrial coatings manufacturer

ManufactureOS: costing and inventory ERP

Product costs lived in spreadsheets. Every formulation change meant recalculating by hand, and stock was checked by walking to the store.

  • Formulation-based cost engine with batch scaling
  • Raw-material inventory, low-stock alerts and RM forecasting
  • Production entry, shift and machine setup, batch PDFs
  • Role-based access with server-side sessions and an audit log
  • Weekly stock report emailed automatically to management
BeforeCosts recalculated by hand after every formulation change; stock checked by walking to the store.
AfterCost and profitability update the moment a formulation changes, with fewer manual errors and live stock on screen.

Enquiry-to-bill CRM for an HR services firm

Client enquiries, bill requests and payments were tracked across separate sheets and email threads, so nobody had the full picture.

  • Role-based logins for admins, managers and staff

Raunaq Paint Industry

Dealer brochure and a formulation-to-quotation ERP

A paint maker with several brands and six shade cards needed one clear story for dealers, and a faster way to price and quote.

  • 8-page dealer brochure: brand journey, range, special finishes
  • 157 shade swatches rebuilt across six shade cards
  • ERP with recipe management and automatic pricing
  • Dealer price-list import with zone and customer-type pricing
  • Quotation and proforma invoice generator
BeforeQuotations took hours to prepare; each brand told its story separately.
AfterQuotations ready in minutes, and dealers get one brochure covering every brand and shade.

I understand the problem because I've worked where it happens

I'm Praveen. Since 2022 I've worked alongside manufacturing and service teams and watched where their hours actually go: copying numbers between sheets, chasing approvals, rebuilding the same report every week.

I trained in mechanical engineering, so I think about how a process runs on the floor, not just how it looks in a meeting. That is where my tools come from: costing engines, CRMs, dashboards and reports that send themselves, each built because a real team needed it.

I work end to end: understanding the process, designing the screens, building the automation and fixing things after launch. My English and Political Science degree is why the documents I write read clearly.

I believe small and mid-sized businesses deserve the same clarity large companies get from their systems, at a size and cost that fits them.
